title: AI Agent Capabilities Are Doubling Every Three Months
channel: The AI Daily Brief: Artificial Intelligence News
summary: AI Daily Brief on METR's 'Moore's law for agents' time-horizon paper and its caveats.

assertions.quote: The length of tasks that AI can do is doubling about every 7 months

verdicts.note: METR's 2025 time-horizon study found ~7-month doubling (faster in 2024-25); later measurements stayed on or above trend, with wide error bars.

METR timed human experts on 170 software and research tasks (HCAST, RE-Bench, SWAA) and regressed 11 frontier models' 50%-success time horizons on release date from 2019 to early 2025, finding a doubling every 207 days (95% CI 166-240); the measurement is the claim's own source, a preprint by the lab, on a fixed benchmark suite at 50% reliability, not real-world work.

assertions.quote: For models created since last year, the doublings in capability are occurring every 3 months

verdicts.note: METR noted a faster ~4-month doubling for 2024-25 models; later data roughly held, though the sample is small and uncertain.

o3 sits above the 2019-2025 trend line (p = 0.006), which the authors say only 'may imply' a faster trend in 2024 and early 2025; one model above the line suggests rather than establishes an acceleration.

Using METR's Time Horizon 1.1 data from 2023 on, Epoch found the log 50% time horizon grew faster than a single linear (constant doubling) trend predicts, best fit by a separate trend for reasoning models that is roughly 2-3x faster; it cannot pin down a precise rate and compares against a 2023-onward fit, not METR's 2019-2025 seven-month doubling.

assertions.quote: increasing the reliability threshold from 50 to 80% reduces the average time horizon by a factor of five

verdicts.note: METR's own analysis: 80%-success horizons are roughly 4-5x shorter than 50% horizons.

On METR's task suite the 80%-success time horizon doubles at a similar rate (204 vs 207 days) but is 4-6x shorter than the 50% horizon, so models that sometimes succeed on hard tasks cannot reliably do tasks of moderate length.

assertions.quote: it appears that exponential is what we have here

verdicts.note: METR's task-horizon metric kept doubling roughly every 7 months through 2025-26 and coding benchmarks rose sharply; perceived per-release gains feel smaller but the trend is steep.
